## Aspect

```java
public class Aspect
```

The aspect registry of TC4: the 48 original aspects plus every aspect an add-on registers. Amounts and centivis are stored by their consumers.

 <h2>Add-on aspects</h2>

An add-on registers an aspect exactly as it did on 1.7.10, by constructing it once:

```java `public static final Aspect TEMPUS = new Aspect("tempus", 0xB68CFF, new Aspect[]{Aspect.VOID, Aspect.ORDER}, ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("myaddon", "textures/aspects/tempus.png"), 1); ThaumcraftApi.registerObjectTag(new ItemStack(Items.CLOCK), new AspectList().add(TEMPUS, 4));`
```

The constructor is the whole registration: the aspect is then known to the thaumometer, the research table, the research notes, essentia storage and transport, the crucible, the alchemical furnace, the centrifuge, phials, crystals, wisps, the creative tab and the EMI/JEI/Jade integrations, exactly like an original aspect. The contract:
- **When.** During mod initialisation, on both physical sides (common code, never only the client or only the server): a `static final` field of a class your initialiser loads (Fabric `ModInitializer#onInitialize`; NeoForge mod constructor or `FMLCommonSetupEvent#enqueueWork`). The order relative to Thaumcraft's own initialiser does not matter: the 48 original aspects are registered by the static initialiser of this class, so they always precede add-on aspects, and every consumer reads this registry when it needs it. Do not register aspects after a world or server started (data pack recipes, open menus and saved data are validated against the registry at that point) and never remove one: the registry has no unregistration.
- **Tag.** Unique, non-empty, lowercase, made of `[a-z0-9_.-]`; a duplicate throws `IllegalArgumentException`. The tag is the identity of the aspect everywhere: saved block entities, item components, player knowledge, research notes, recipes and every packet store the tag string, and EMI/JEI use `thaumcraft:<tag>` as identifier (a tag that is not a valid resource path is accepted, as in the original, but logged, because those identifiers then fail). Changing a tag later orphans existing worlds.
- **Components.** A compound has exactly two registered parents; any other array length makes the aspect primal (`isPrimal()`, original rule). The research table and the hex notes link an aspect to its two parents; `getCombinationResult` answers the first registered aspect with that pair, so a pair that an original aspect already uses never yields the add-on aspect. An aspect without components (`null`) is a primal: like the six original primals it is given to a player on the first join (original ResearchManager.loadPlayerData), but wand, sceptre and amulet vis, vis relays, shards, crystal clusters and infused ores of this port exist for the six original primals only.
- **Texture.** `getImage()` is bound directly as a texture, not as an atlas sprite: ship `assets/<namespace>/textures/aspects/<name>.png`, a square image (the originals are 32x32 RGBA) drawn white or grey on transparency, because Thaumcraft tints it with `getColor()` (RGB `0xRRGGBB`, no alpha). Use the five-argument constructor with your own namespace; the three- and four-argument forms derive `thaumcraft:textures/aspects/<lowercase tag>.png`, which only the original aspects ship.
- **Blend.** `1` (additive, the default) or `771` (alpha blended, the dark aspects), used by nodes and aspect orbs; other values render as additive.
- **Chat colour.** One legacy formatting code character (for example `"5"`), used for primal vis costs of foci; the compound constructors default it to `"f"`.
- **Language keys.** `getName()` is the capitalised tag and is not translated, as in the original. Add `tc.aspect.<tag>` (the meaning shown under the name, for example `"tc.aspect.tempus": "Time"`) and `tc.aspect.help.<tag>` (a short lowercase noun used by the thaumometer when the aspect is a missing parent: "To understand this you need to study %s.") to your own `assets/<namespace>/lang/en_us.json`.
- **Networking.** Client and server must register the same aspects: a client that lacks one cannot decode the phials, crystals, wisp essence, jar labels, recipes and research notes that name it and is disconnected. The essentia tube vent effect and the deconstruction table menu send a position in the registry order, and the thaumatorium menu a position in the tag-sorted registry, so register the same aspects in a deterministic order on both sides.
- **Threads.** Registration synchronises on `aspects`, so parallel mod construction (NeoForge) cannot corrupt the map, and `getPrimalAspects()`, `getCompoundAspects()` and `getCombinationResult` read it under the same lock. Code that iterates `aspects` itself while other mods may still be constructing must synchronise on it too.

## AspectEventProxy

```java
public class AspectEventProxy
```

The original TC4 aspect registration facade.

The native port keeps the TC4 registry in `ThaumcraftApi`; this proxy only forwards to it so that an add-on written against the TC6 shape keeps compiling.

<a id="aspecteventproxy-registerobjecttag"></a>
```java
public void registerObjectTag(ItemStack item, AspectList aspects)
```

Registers the aspects of one item identity.

<a id="aspecteventproxy-registerobjecttag-2"></a>
```java
public void registerObjectTag(ItemStack item, int[] meta, AspectList aspects)
```

Registers one item identity for a group of metadata values.

<a id="aspecteventproxy-registerobjecttag-3"></a>
```java
public void registerObjectTag(String nativeItemTag, AspectList aspects)
```

Registers every member of a native item tag.

Native namespaced item tags replace Forge ore names; legacy names require an explicit mapping.

<a id="aspecteventproxy-registercomplexobjecttag"></a>
```java
public void registerComplexObjectTag(ItemStack item, AspectList aspects)
```

Registers the aspects of one item identity, including its recipe-derived base.

<a id="aspecteventproxy-registercomplexobjecttag-2"></a>
```java
public void registerComplexObjectTag(String nativeItemTag, AspectList aspects)
```

Registers every member of a native item tag, including its recipe-derived base.

This TC6-shaped convenience overload applies TC4's complex-item registration to each native tag member. It requires the loaded server recipe lifecycle, preserves the original existing-tag branch, and copies additions per member. Legacy Forge ore names require an explicit mapping.

## AspectList

```java
public class AspectList implements Serializable
```

TC4's ordered aspect amounts. add sums; merge takes the maximum.

```java
public final LinkedHashMap<Aspect, Integer> aspects
```

<a id="aspectlist-aspectlist"></a>
```java
public AspectList(ItemStack stack)
```

Original AspectList:25-36 - the object aspects of an item stack. Null/empty stacks are passed to the handler; Exceptions are swallowed (retaining any amounts already copied), but Errors escape.

The original wrapped the call in a try/catch and kept an empty list when the add-on surface threw; the native keeps the same behaviour.

<a id="aspectlist-getaspectssortedamount"></a>
```java
public Aspect[] getAspectsSortedAmount()
```

Original AspectList.getAspectsSortedAmount:100-123: the aspects are sorted by decreasing amount, but an aspect without an amount never moves and equal amounts keep their declared order.

<a id="aspectlist-getaspectssortedbyamount"></a>
```java
public Aspect[] getAspectsSortedByAmount()
```

Returns a new key array using `getAspectsSortedAmount()`; never changes the stored order.

<a id="aspectlist-add"></a>
```java
public AspectList add(Aspect aspect, int amount)
```

The original addition: the amount of an aspect grows by the added one. Null aspects are ignored; signed amounts are summed without overflow checks.

Forced 1.21.1 change (documented deviation from the original): the original stored the aspect under its own key, so a `null` aspect - the aspect of an unknown tag that `Aspect.getAspect(String)` answered for - became a key of the map (oracle `thaumcraft/api/aspects/AspectList.java`, the `add` method has no null check). The original then crashed with a `NullPointerException` in `getPrimalAspects`, which calls `isPrimal()` on every key without a null check. The native port drops a `null` aspect instead, so an item of another mod never takes the whole aspect list down; the amount of an unknown tag is then not counted by `size()` and not answered by `getAmount(Aspect)`.

<a id="aspectlist-add-2"></a>
```java
public AspectList add(AspectList other)
```

Adds other's amounts into this receiver and returns this; null other throws NPE, and units are not converted.

<a id="aspectlist-merge"></a>
```java
public AspectList merge(Aspect aspect, int amount)
```

Stores the maximum existing/supplied signed amount and returns this; null aspect is ignored, with no unit conversion.

<a id="aspectlist-merge-2"></a>
```java
public AspectList merge(AspectList other)
```

Merges each amount by maximum into this receiver and returns this; null other throws NPE.

<a id="aspectlist-reduce"></a>
```java
public boolean reduce(Aspect aspect, int amount)
```

Subtracts amount in the list's units, retaining a zero key; null aspect, negative amount or insufficient stock returns false unchanged.

<a id="aspectlist-remove"></a>
```java
public AspectList remove(Aspect aspect, int amount)
```

Subtracts amount in the list's units and removes nonpositive stock; null aspect/negative amount is ignored, returning this.

<a id="aspectlist-remove-2"></a>
```java
public AspectList remove(Aspect aspect)
```

Removes the key (null is allowed by the map) and returns this; no other state changes.

<a id="aspectlist-reducetoprimals"></a>
```java
public AspectList reduceToPrimals(boolean merge)
```

Returns a new recursive primal decomposition, preserving amount units; merge uses maxima within each level, not global deduplication.

<a id="aspectlist-writetonbt"></a>
```java

```

Writes amounts without unit conversion to tag's Aspects list; null tag throws NPE.

<a id="aspectlist-writetonbt-2"></a>
```java
public void writeToNBT(CompoundTag tag, String label)
```

Replaces tag's named list with aspect tags and signed amounts; tag/label must be non-null, and this list is unchanged.

<a id="aspectlist-readfromnbt"></a>
```java
public void readFromNBT(CompoundTag tag)
```

Clears this receiver and reads tag's Aspects list; null tag throws NPE after clearing.

<a id="aspectlist-readfromnbt-2"></a>
```java
public void readFromNBT(CompoundTag tag, String label)
```

Clears this receiver and adds named-list amounts unchanged; unknown aspect names are dropped, missing lists read empty, and tag/label must be non-null.

## AspectRegistryEvent

```java
public class AspectRegistryEvent
```

The aspect registration event of the original add-on surface.

Forced 1.21.1 change: Forge's `net.minecraftforge.fml.common.eventhandler.Event` does not exist in 1.21.1, so the event is a plain object that add-ons subscribe to with `addListener(Consumer)` and that the mod raises with `post()`. The published `register` proxy keeps the original registration surface.

<a id="aspectregistryevent-register"></a>
```java
public final AspectEventProxy register
```

The registration proxy the original event exposed.

<a id="aspectregistryevent-addlistener"></a>
```java
public static void addListener(Consumer<AspectRegistryEvent> listener)
```

Ignores null listeners; other listeners run in registration order without registration-time validation.

<a id="aspectregistryevent-removelistener"></a>
```java
public static void removeListener(Consumer<AspectRegistryEvent> listener)
```

Unsubscribes a previously added listener.

<a id="aspectregistryevent-listenercount"></a>
```java
public static int listenerCount()
```

The number of registered listeners; a listener may unregister itself while the event runs.

<a id="aspectregistryevent-post"></a>
```java
public static void post()
```

Logs listener RuntimeExceptions and continues; Errors escape, and null listeners cannot be registered here.

## AspectSourceHelper

```java
public class AspectSourceHelper
```

The original TC4 essentia source helper.

Oracle `thaumcraft/api/aspects/AspectSourceHelper.java:21-39` published two static helpers that reached `thaumcraft.common.lib.events.EssentiaHandler` by reflection. The handler looked for ANY `IAspectSource` around the tile and honoured both the direction and the range: the drain took one unit of the aspect out of the first source that held it (oracle `EssentiaHandler:49-56`) and the search asked every source whether it held the aspect (oracle `EssentiaHandler:71-78`).

Forced 1.21.1 change: `ForgeDirection` became `Direction` and the reflective lookup became a direct call, because the native handler owns the search itself. The unknown direction of 1.7.10 has no native counterpart and is written as a `null` direction. The search is the original one: `EssentiaSourceSearch` walks the same half box in the same order.

<a id="aspectsourcehelper-drainessentia"></a>
```java
public static boolean drainEssentia(BlockEntity tile, Aspect aspect, Direction direction, int range)
```

The original `drainEssentia`: one unit of the aspect is taken out of the first source of the search that holds it.

The original sent its essence flow packet to the players around the tile (oracle `EssentiaHandler:54`); the native sends the same packet through `thaumcraft.common.lib.network.EssentiaFlowFxNetworking`.

<a id="aspectsourcehelper-findessentia"></a>
```java
public static boolean findEssentia(BlockEntity tile, Aspect aspect, Direction direction, int range)
```

The original `findEssentia`: true when any source of the search holds the aspect.

Oracle `EssentiaHandler:76` asks the source with `doesContainerContainAmount(aspect, 1)`.

```java
public interface IAspectContainer
```

TC4's aspect-container contract. addToContainer returns the unaccepted remainder.

boolean doesContainerAccept(Aspect aspect)
int addToContainer(Aspect aspect, int amount)

```

Legacy multi-aspect removal with implementation-specific support; native nodes return false even for null.

**Deprecated:** Use takeFromContainer(Aspect, int) in aspect units; a caller loop is not an atomic transaction.

```java
boolean doesContainerContainAmount(Aspect aspect, int amount)
```

<a id="iaspectcontainer-doescontainercontain"></a>
```java
boolean doesContainerContain(AspectList aspects)
```

> **Deprecated.**

Legacy multi-aspect containment query; native nodes return false even for null rather than implementing an all/any test.

**Deprecated:** Query doesContainerContainAmount(Aspect, int) for each required aspect to express all-of semantics explicitly; implementations may reject queries.

```java
int containerContains(Aspect aspect)
```
